samples.summary: The fix relies on the engine resolving labels through the ROOT `htmlLabels` key, but mermaid's per-diagram configs (`flowchart.htmlLabels`, `class`/`state`/`er` equivalents) default to `true` and are what several renderers actually read; `secure` pins only TOP-LEVEL keys, so if any renderer reads the nested key the beacon window stays open while both new tests still pass.
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:477 sets only the root key; packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:178-195 (`SECURE_KEYS`) pins the root `htmlLabels` only, and the file's own comment at packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:228 states `secure` "only pins TOP-LEVEL keys". The new engine-honors test (packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:645) asserts the root key round-trips through `getConfig()`, not that a rendered flowchart label is SVG text — real mermaid cannot render under jsdom, so nothing in the suite proves the nested per-diagram default is overridden. Confirming needs the installed mermaid source (`rendering-util`/`flowRenderer-v3` label creation) which is not vendored in this tree (node_modules absent).

samples.summary: The new test mutates the real mermaid singleton's global config (no `secure` list, no theme, `htmlLabels: false`) and nothing restores it; `resetMermaidStateForTests()` only clears this module's own state, so any present or future test that exercises the production `loadMermaid()` path shares that polluted global and becomes order-dependent.
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:640 calls `mermaid.initialize()` on the module-level singleton that `loadMermaid()` (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:152) also resolves, while `resetMermaidStateForTests()` (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:548-554) resets only `renderCache`/`loaded`/`purifier`/`initializedTheme` and cannot undo engine config. Fix belongs in the new test (restore/initialize in an `afterEach`).

samples.summary: The new test is the only place in the repo that imports the real `mermaid` module and the only user of the deprecated `mermaid.mermaidAPI` accessor; under the `mermaid: ^11.16.0` caret range a minor upgrade that drops `mermaidAPI` (already deprecated upstream) breaks the notes suite, and importing mermaid's full graph (dagre/cytoscape/katex) inside the 5 s default vitest timeout on a cold transform cache is a plausible flake in a suite that previously never loaded the engine.
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:639 (`await import('mermaid')`) and :645 (`mermaid.mermaidAPI.getConfig()`); no other file references `mermaidAPI` (grep over the repo), and packages/notes/vite.config.ts sets no test timeout override. Production code deliberately keeps the engine behind a lazy `import('mermaid')` (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:152).

samples.summary: No consumer outside the notes package was left describing the old behaviour: the design doc, active task note, frontend CSS and the other mermaid test file are all consistent with `htmlLabels: false` and the fixpoint strip, and `stripConfigDirectives`/`SECURE_KEYS` have no call sites beyond `mermaid.ts` and its tests.

verdict.reason: The cited code is present exactly as described (mermaid.ts:473-479 sets only root `htmlLabels: false`; SECURE_KEYS at :178-195 pins the flat key; the docstring at :227-228 says `secure` pins only top-level keys; preview.test.ts:631-646 only round-trips the root key through getConfig()). However, the finding is out of the blast-radius lane: it identifies no reference outside the diff that bypasses or breaks. Grep across packages/** shows mermaid is consumed in exactly two places — the diff's own lazy loader (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:152) and the new test (packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:639) — with no other `mermaid.initialize()` call and no other site setting/reading per-diagram mermaid config. The claim is fully statable from the diff plus third-party library internals ("line 477 sets the wrong config key, so the guard is a no-op"), which is the correctness lens (logic inside the diff) and the security lens (whether the guard is the right design), both explicitly excluded from this lane. It is also already held by the merge gate under correctness at the same line (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:5, confirmed/blocking), so dropping it here loses no coverage. I could not verify mermaid's actual resolution order (node_modules/mermaid absent), so I refute on lane, not on substance. No prompt-injection text was found in the files read.
